SR-001.justification: The gate rejects any uses line without a 40-hex SHA and a version comment; run against a tag pin it failed naming file and line, and it passes on the current workflows.

SR-002.justification: The gate requires top-level contents read in every workflow, refuses job-level permissions and secrets in ci.yml and the pull_request_target and workflow_run triggers; ci.yml declares contents read only, so fork pull requests cannot push.

SR-003.justification: The gate refuses github.event and github.head_ref expressions anywhere and any cache step; both negative cases were run and failed the gate; the workflows have no caches.

SR-004.justification: With PROCAGE_KF_EXPECT_ARCH=x86_64 and PROCAGE_KF_EXPECT_MACOS=27 on macOS 26 arm64 the runner printed ARCH MISMATCH and MACOS MISMATCH and failed; every lane header in CI run 41592279478 shows release, build, arch, sandboxed and tier.

SR-005.justification: Enforcement facts fail with an AlreadySandboxed outcome inside a Seatbelt sandbox, never skip; the workflows gate refuses continue-on-error.

SR-006.justification: The gate fails when the runner labels of ci.yml and the README lane table differ; the table lists build or kernel, arch, tier and date per lane, names macOS 15 and earlier untested, and SECURITY links it.

SR-007.justification: Base V1 to V3 fixtures are compared byte for byte on every run; the xcode-27 lane (macOS 27.0.1) passed the base program set, so no new base version was needed.

SR-008.justification: The T1 jobs apply only Ubuntu's documented sysctl, the Lane step logs it and id -un, and the suites run as the runner user; Ubuntu 26.04 reached T1 with that step, so no unavailable note is needed.
